author: Judy D.J. Ellich
title: Somerset Night Out a playground connection just before schools start - NewsBreak
text:
By Judy D.J. Ellich ,
18 hours ago SOMERSET — The rain held off. Somerset Night Out was a success. And $5 gave the local fire department bragging rights.
We were thrilled," said Jody M. Gearhart, Clerk, Somerset Borough Police Department , about the event recently held at the Union Street Playground in Somerset Borough that drew a large, light-hearted family-oriented crowd.
The event is coordinated by the Somerset Borough Police Department and the Village at Somerset.
"We began fundraising for this event in January 2026, expanding our reach to other areas within the county," Gearhart said. "Without sponsors, this event would not be possible."
Among the local businesses, groups and individuals also who jumped in to help with the community event were Patriot Village, Somerset Healthcare & Rehab and Casselman Healthcare & Rehab sponsors of the huge event tent on the basketball court in the playground. Martin’s Oil/Convenience Store donated 73 pizzas; while Sheetz stores and Roof Garden Market donated over 600 hot dogs and buns.
The list of sponsors "could go on and on," Gearhart said.
It's Showtime Somerset Regional Volunteer Fire Department Fire Chief Jim Clark challenged the Somerset Borough Police Department's Chief Richard Appel on Facebook Live to see who could raise the most money for the Union Street Playground by being a participant in the new feature, the dunk tank, for this annual event.
The rules included individuals pay $5 for three balls or $20 to walk up and push the paddle for the one they wanted to dunk. The volunteer fire department earned bragging rights by raising $235 to the borough police's $230, Gearhart said.
"Night Out is all about the community we serve. Some serve as law enforcement, and others serve in emergency services or specialized organizations. People in our community don’t realize how many other agencies assist law enforcement and emergency services," she said
Somerset Night Out is designed to introduce the community to everyone involved with keeping them safe. Fire trucks filled the front apron at the volunteer firehall as bounce houses filled with children took over the apparatus bay in the fire department for the event.
'It’s important for the community, especially young children, to know that law enforcement is there to help them and that they can trust them," Gearhart said.
One of the goals of Somerset Night Out is to help "the community understand that those who serve in this capacity have families and live within the community they serve," Gearhart said.
The 2026 event also was an opportunity to recognize "a very special lady, retired Somerset Borough Police Det. Ruth Beckner," she said. Appel presented Beckner with a Retired Detective Badge and thanked her for her 33 years in law enforcement, including 28 with the Somerset Borough Police Department.
This article originally appeared on The Daily American: Somerset Night Out a playground connection just before schools start
